_schema_note: 1.2.0 (Codex R1 P3, 2026-06-03): per-rung `verdict` REMOVED. A convergence rung is an OBSERVATION on the refinement branch, not a case verdict — marking the 216-element rung (residual 3.47% > the 3% case tolerance) as PASS was a per-rung honesty mismatch. The single case-level PASS verdict lives ONLY in the sibling cross_check_verdict.yaml (the canonical 40x20x6 / 4800-element solve, residual +1.08%). Each point now carries an honest `within_case_tolerance` flag instead.
notes: NAFEMS LE10 sigma_yy at point D (2.0, 0, +0.3), upper surface, vs the published -5.38 MPa. Real ccx 2.23, full-integration C3D20, mid-plane frame. Convergence is MONOTONE from above on the refined branch (216 -> 4800 elements): residual falls +3.47% -> +1.08% as the mesh refines. The canonical 40x20x6 / 4800-element solve (+1.08%) is the only rung INSIDE the 3% case tolerance and is the one carrying the case PASS verdict (in cross_check_verdict.yaml); the coarser rungs are convergence-branch evidence, NOT passing verdicts. A constant refinement ratio Richardson extrapolation is NOT reported because the mesh ladder uses non-constant (nc,nr,nt) ratios (transfinite structured hex); the monotone decreasing residual toward the canonical 5.38 MPa magnitude is the convergence evidence. Coarser meshes below 216 el (e.g. 8x4x2 = 64 el, +3.02%; 6x3x2 = 36 el, +1.45%) are non-monotonic coarse-mesh artifacts at the sharp inner-edge stress and are excluded from the convergence branch.
